papers.summary: Introduces spectral weight decay as a decoupled nuclear-norm update that shrinks smaller singular values, lowers effective rank, improves low-rank compression, and can improve robustness to label noise.
papers.relevance: Directly matches spectral regularization, effective rank, low-rank compressibility, compression-quality tradeoffs, and noisy-label generalization.

evidence.quote: Spectral weight decay lowers the effective rank of weight matrices, making them amenable to low-rank compression.
At 500 M and a 4% distortion budget, it supports 1.89× compression, compared with 1.14× after standard weight decay.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Proposes Learnable Subspace Projections, which learn low-rank subspaces end-to-end against the dense model's outputs or training loss while keeping pretrained weights frozen.
papers.relevance: Strong match for low-rank compression, global rank allocation, and model-quality versus memory/throughput tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: We introduce Learnable Subspace Projections (LSP), which instead learns the subspaces to discard end-to-end.

papers.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression

papers.summary: Presents sMuon, an efficient approximation of Muon for low-rank adapters, evaluated in supervised fine-tuning and ReLoRA pretraining.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization for LoRA and low-rank parameterizations, including practical Muon approximations.

evidence.quote: Our method, sMuon (small Muon), performs favourably across SFT and a ReLoRA pretraining experiment.

papers.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

papers.summary: Introduces NoRA, which normalizes LoRA down-projection matrices during training or only at initialization to improve convergence, stability, performance, and forgetting behavior.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to LoRA optimization geometry and training dynamics across pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

evidence.quote: We introduce Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation (NoRA), a simple yet effective method that normalizes the down-projection matrices during training.

papers.title: Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Introduces NorMuon, combining Muon orthogonalization with neuron-wise normalization and an efficient distributed FSDP2 implementation.
papers.relevance: Relevant to optimizer design, Newton-Schulz-style orthogonalization, scalable LLM training, and efficiency comparisons.

evidence.quote: NorMuon addresses this imbalance by maintaining second-order momentum statistics for each neuron and applying row-wise normalization after orthogonalization.

papers.title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable

papers.summary: Shows that optimizer rankings and scaling behavior can change with batch size, attributing this to gradient-noise and curvature-dependent bias-variance effects.
papers.relevance: Useful for understanding optimizer and training-efficiency tradeoffs across regimes, especially for language-model pretraining.

evidence.quote: the best optimizer for language model pretraining changes with batch size even after extensive hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: The Best Optimizer Depends on Batch Size

papers.summary: Introduces Sharpness-Aware Minimization and reports improved generalization and robustness to label noise across models and benchmarks.
papers.relevance: Directly matches the user's interest in generalization, memorization, optimization geometry, and noisy-label training.

evidence.quote: SAM natively provides robustness to label noise on par with that provided by state-of-the-art procedures that specifically target learning with noisy labels.

papers.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization

papers.summary: Analyzes convergence failures of SAM under generalized smoothness and proposes Curvature-Scaled SAM with bounded distortion guarantees.
papers.relevance: Provides theory for optimization stability and convergence beyond standard smoothness assumptions.

evidence.quote: we propose Curvature-Scaled SAM (CS-SAM), which scales both the perturbation and the descent step by suitable curvature upper bounds

papers.title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness

papers.summary: Introduces context language models that manage context as editable files and reports efficiency and accuracy gains for context-management and multi-agent tasks.
papers.relevance: Strong match for the user's goal of building an AI research-digest agent with explicit context management and agent-controlled memory.

evidence.quote: We introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), language models that natively manage their own context.

papers.title: Context Language Models

papers.summary: Reviews reasoning-search systems through retrieval coupling, controller design, knowledge sources, grounding, verification, and stopping behavior.
papers.relevance: Directly supports the design of a research-digest agent with iterative retrieval, structured decisions, evidence integration, and verification.

evidence.quote: interleaving planning, querying, retrieval, integration, verification, and stopping.

papers.title: Reasoning-Search-Augmented LLMs: An Operational Taxonomy, Benchmark Analysis and Controlled Evidence Synthesis
